horizontally stacked rows or registers of repeated marks

justification: The only real correspondence is generic: both surfaces carry rows of small repeated schematic marks (crew strokes on boat hulls in A, rows of small signs and figures in B) stacked in roughly horizontal registers, rendered as simple outline forms. Otherwise the content is wholly different: A shows nothing but long curved-prowed boats with stroke crews on an open rock face, while B shows a formal composition of standing figures worshipping a rayed disc above dense ordered lines of script and framed name-groups.
